name: Allo
description: A mobile-first business phone system (numbers, dialer, call recording, CRM sync with HubSpot/Salesforce, AI call notes) that pitches itself as a cheaper, consumer-grade RingCentral/Aircall replacement. It's the first product of the "Mobile First Company" holding of ex-Spendesk growth lead Jérémy Goillot, whose stated vision is affordable software "for the most boring businesses" like retail and services (company-stated).

mentions.evidence: ARR ~$3M (Apr 2026) ← $1M (Oct 2025) · target $10M by end-2026 5,000 customers · ~750 signups/week · >35% trial→paid · ARPU $160/mo (from $18/mo at launch) 17 staff · $18.5M raised (incl. $13M seed Oct 2025 at >50x revenue) >30% of acquisition from Google keywords (competitor + feature terms) and long-form SEO; "best call recording software" post ~2,100 organic clicks/mo
mentions.indieAngle: It's VC-funded, but the lesson is cheap: "Aircall but for one trade." In Poland that could be a VoIP number + call log + missed-call SMS-back for gabinety/warsztaty, integrated with Booksy/Versum, at ~59 zł/mo per line.

whyItPrints: Telephony is a replacement category: every SMB already pays for phones. Allo found that users who make more than 5 calls basically never churn. About 50% of new revenue comes from seat expansion.
whyThisMatters:
A shop already pays for a phone. Allo sells a number, a dialer, call recording, and notes, and it can sync the call to HubSpot or Salesforce. The pitch is a cheaper version of the big business-phone brands, aimed at retail and services. It is the first product of a holding company started by someone who used to run growth at Spendesk.

The founder says people who make more than a handful of calls almost never leave, and that about half of new revenue is extra seats. Thousands of customers. A trial converts often. The average account pays much more than the launch price. Seventeen people. A large seed round landed in late 2025. A lot of the signups come from search. The yearly number is from an April 2026 interview. It is not a Stripe connection.

You pay so the work calls are not on a personal phone.
